A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETTFS research framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification accuracies, inference latency measurements and component analyses on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 and DVS Gesture.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds CIFAR100 results, additional comparisons, energy estimates and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The AMOS masking and forced final spike, ETTFS initialization distribution, affine weight normalization, temporal decoding rules and average-pooling remain unchanged. Pre-trained-weight experiments are additional evaluation configurations; v3 specifies no revised ETTFS algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR100's 100-class image classification task while retaining all four previous datasets. This extends coverage within the existing vision classification domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds DTA-TTFS to the accuracy and latency comparisons in Tables 1–2, distinguishing pre-trained and reproduced results. It also introduces rate-coded SNN comparisons for energy in Table 3 and architecture-matched accuracy in Appendix Table 7. These substantially broaden the comparator set; earlier accuracy-table comparators remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ReLU pre-training conditions, time-step and initialization-variance sweeps, and three energy estimation protocols with CMOS, TrueNorth and SpikeSim assumptions. The original batch sizes, optimizers, training budgets, losses and augmentations remain unchanged between v2 Table 6 and v3 Table 8.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix A systematically tests two previously fixed choices: time-steps from 2 to 12 and initialization variance from 0.25 to 4 across three datasets. Table 4 also adds an initialization-only ablation. Earlier gradient, depth, normalization, training-curve and decoder-decay analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates, whereas v3 Table 1 adds ± values to ETTFS accuracies, including retained results. Their meaning, repeated-run counts and seeds are unspecified. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, but not an increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: The original four-dataset headline accuracies and latencies remain. v3 adds CIFAR100 accuracy of 70.27% without pre-training and 72.70% with pre-training, plus pre-trained CIFAR10 accuracy of 93.89%, energy estimates and new comparison and ablation entries. These are additional conditions, not same-setting gains. The introduction's CIFAR100 value of 70.29% conflicts with Table 1.

T1.justification: v3 Equation 12 corrects v2 Equation 9's unsupported reduction of input-current expectation to the weight mean. Equations 14–17 explicitly formulate time-averaged per-neuron variance instead of the earlier tensor-level derivation, while yielding the same initialization distribution. The pooling derivations are retained in the main text.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the state-of-the-art claim from TTFS SNNs generally to step-by-step TTFS SNNs and extend it to CIFAR100. The conclusion specifies directly trained TTFS SNNs. The four principal framework contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking causal-model expressivity to available temporal inputs and DVS difficulty to motion encoding, and explicitly discusses small-dataset limitations. It removes v2's GPU post-spike-resting caveat. Its new claim that unit variance consistently outperforms smaller values conflicts with Fashion-MNIST's better result at 0.5 in Table 6.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code/log repository address and discloses a single RTX 4090 with 24GB memory. It documents the CIFAR100 classifier output but removes architecture output-size columns and the 800-feature linear-layer expansion detail. The main hyperparameter table is retained; added pre-training and CIFAR100 settings remain incompletely documented.

R1.justification: v3 substantially contracts the biological coding and broader SNN literature discussion, including removing Stanojevic's TTFS references and Salimans/Huang normalization references. It adds DTA-TTFS and energy-evaluation literature, with substantive positioning around pre-training requirements, propagation causality and hardware energy costs.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively condensed and rewritten. A Preliminary section is introduced, background and derivations move into the main text, and the ablation narrative and appendices are reorganized. Author/correspondence information, conference front matter, acknowledgements and an impact statement also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is rearranged side by side, the AMOS diagram is redrawn and moved into the main text, and decoder/pooling figures are merged. Tables gain new columns, comparison rows and reporting structures; earlier appendix numerical tables disappear while corresponding plots remain. Training and decay plots shrink from full width to one column, with revised axes and legends.

improvement.justification: The corrected initialization derivation, narrower headline claims and expanded comparator and sensitivity evidence make v3 more precise and better supported. The gains are limited by undefined ± reporting, incomplete documentation of new experimental conditions and a variance-superiority interpretation contradicted by Table 6. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
